aldo-pena.title: Aldo Peña — Digital Artist Archive
aldo-pena.description: UX/UI design and frontend development of a digital artist archive to preserve, organise and explore artworks, career history and documentation.

hero.title: Aldo Peña — Digital Artist Archive
hero.subtitle: UX/UI design and frontend development of a digital platform to preserve, organise and make Aldo Peña’s work, career and legacy accessible.

origin.title: From a website showcasing artworks to a digital archive preserving an artist’s career.
origin.content: The initiative began as a digital space to bring together and showcase Aldo Peña’s work. Reviewing the volume and variety of material — artworks, career history, teaching, multidisciplinary practice and historical documentation — revealed a broader challenge: designing an archive that could organise, connect and make an extensive career accessible, beyond a simple gallery.

context.problema: The archive brings together very different types of content: artworks, documentation, career history, professional practice and historical material. The main UX challenge was to structure this information so people could explore it without excessive fragmentation or losing the connections between content.
context.objetivo: Design a clear, scalable digital archive where works can be explored by category and each piece retains its context through information, images and related records. The structure needed to accommodate new material over time without rethinking the experience.
usuario: People interested in the artist’s work and career
Researchers and people working in the arts and cultural sector
People who need to explore a large archive while keeping their place in the navigation

decisiones: Rethink a website originally intended to showcase artworks as a digital archive designed to grow
Organise an extensive career through clear, progressively detailed information architecture
Connect artworks, biography, multidisciplinary practice and archival material within one coherent experience
Enable artwork exploration through categories, filters and sorting
Keep each piece in context through images, metadata and related records
Build a structure that can gradually accommodate new material

sitemap.title: Architecture for an extensive career
sitemap.description: The first decision was to organise the content into broad areas within a shared experience: Biography, Works, Multidisciplinary Practice, and Legacy and Archive. This avoids isolating every type of material on a separate page and lets visitors move from an overview to increasingly specific content.

interaction.title: Explore the work while keeping its context
interaction.description: The works archive was designed as an exploration tool, rather than a static gallery. Visitors can browse pieces by category, filters and sorting criteria, while progressive loading accommodates a growing collection without overwhelming the interface.

responsive.title: From design to a system ready to grow
responsive.description: The interface was built in React and adapts to different screen sizes. Data services query Supabase to retrieve artworks, categories, images and associated exhibitions. Images are served from Supabase Storage, and multidisciplinary practice has its own queries for projects and documentation.

artworkExperience.title: Explore a piece without leaving the archive
artworkExperience.description: Each artwork can be explored in a modal within the archive. Visitors can browse images, move to the previous or next artwork, and consult the available metadata. The selected artwork is reflected in the URL so a direct link to that piece can be shared.
artworkExperience.alt: Artwork details within the digital artist archive

result.title: An archive ready to grow
result.content: The implementation includes an artwork archive with categories and sorting, artwork details with images and metadata, and a multidisciplinary practice section with projects and associated documentation. Artwork and practice queries are connected to Supabase. The archive remains in development: the Legacy and Archive section currently displays a coming-soon page.

learnings: Designing for large volumes of content means thinking about relationships and architecture before screens.
Separating data, logic and presentation allows an interface to evolve independently of the archive’s final size.
In a cultural archive, interaction should support exploration without visually competing with the artwork.
